name: Sanctum Guardian

source.title: Pathfinder Adventure Path: Bastion of Blasphemies

items.name: Dooming Touch
items.text: The tomb giant's claws carry the accursed power of their foul gods. A creature hit by the tomb giant's claw Strike becomes Doomed 1.

items.name: Font of Death
items.text: The tomb giant turns the spiritual tide on a creature that has just died, temporarily transforming it into a volatile vessel powered by the Void. The tomb giant touches a creature that died within the past 24 hours, infusing its flesh and bone with void energy. Once during the next hour, the tomb giant can spend a single action (from any distance) to release this void from the corpse in an explosion that deals 10d8 void damage in a 15-foot burst (DC 32 basic Fortitude save save); if not released before the end of the hour, the energy dissipates harmlessly. The tomb giant can't use Font of Death while a previous corpse remains infused.

items.name: Pallid Curse
items.text:
Frequency once per day

Trigger A sanctum guardian deals void damage on a creature within 30 feet

---
Effect The void damage scars the target's soul, infecting it with Urgathoa's presence. The target must attempt a DC 32 Fortitude save save with the following effects.

---
Critical Success The target suffers no additional effect.

Success The target becomes Sickened 1 and gains weakness to void 5 until the end of its next turn.

Effect: Pallid Curse (Success)

Failure The target becomes Sickened 2 and gains weakness to void 5; this weakness has an unlimited duration. If the target dies while this curse remains in effect, the curse ends, but the target automatically rises as an undead creature (the GM picks one of the same level as the target) that goes on to serve Urgathoa in its unlife. If the target is destroyed in its new undead form, it reverts to its original living form but is Dying 3.

Effect: Pallid Curse (Failure)

Critical Failure As failure, but weakness to void 10.

text:
Masters of mausoleums and keepers of crypts, the dread creatures called tomb giants are anathema to all living beings, but especially so to other types of giants. Long ago, so the legends say, tomb giants sold their souls in exchange for unfathomable power over the undead. Tomb giants construct massive gothic settlements in haunted valleys and on forsaken hillsides, far enough away from the societies of smaller people that they remain relatively undisturbed, but close enough that they can raid the graveyards of nearby villages with impunity. Elder tomb giants enjoy the thrill of subduing, slaying, and reanimating their fellow giants. A tomb giant views its mortal life as only one part of its existence. After death, most tomb giants are reanimated as undead, who then continue to practice their necromantic arts.

---
Spread across the world, giants are as diverse as the isolated places they inhabit. A giant makes a big impression on the local environment, especially on smaller and weaker creatures.
